intro: This question helps us find the best place for you to begin.

widget.instructions: Add each force with Precise controls, choose who exerts it, then drag its tip (or type its size and direction). The amber arrow is the net force; press Play to see the motion your diagram predicts.

stem: A {{m}} kg box is pulled across a rough floor by a rope at {{ang}}° above the horizontal. The rope's tension is {{T}} N and the box moves at a constant 1.5 m/s. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
Draw every force acting on the box, with its direction and size.
answerText: Weight {{W}} N down (Earth); normal force {{N}} N up (floor); tension {{T}} N at {{ang}}° (rope); friction {{f}} N backwards (floor)

hints.text: List what touches the box: the floor and the rope. Gravity acts too. Each gives one or two forces.
Constant speed means the net force is zero. Watch the amber net-force arrow and press Play: the box should neither speed up nor slow down.
Vertically: N + T sin {{ang}}° = mg. Horizontally: friction = T cos {{ang}}°.

missing-normal.text: Without the normal force, your diagram predicts the box sinks through the floor: watch it drift away from the real box. The floor pushes up on the box.

missing-weight.text: Every body near the Earth has a weight, pulling straight down.

missing-tension.text: The rope pulls the box along its own direction, {{ang}}° above the horizontal.

missing-friction.text: Without friction, the rope's forward pull would make the box speed up, as your prediction shows. The rough floor opposes the sliding.

extra-force-of-motion.text: The box keeps moving because of inertia; there is no separate 'force of motion', and nothing pushes it. Every force needs an agent touching the box (or gravity).

normal-equals-weight.text: The rope pulls partly upward, so the floor doesn't need to push as hard: N = mg − T sin {{ang}}° = {{N}} N.

constant-velocity-unbalanced.text: At constant velocity the forces balance, so friction equals the rope's horizontal pull, T cos {{ang}}° = {{f}} N. Your prediction shows the box speeding up or slowing down.

normal-direction.text: The normal force is perpendicular to the floor, straight up.

tension-direction.text: Tension acts along the rope, at {{ang}}° above the horizontal.

friction-direction.text: Friction on a sliding box points opposite its motion, backwards.

double-counted-force.text: Each agent gives each kind of force only once. Remove the duplicate.

force-direction.text: Check the direction of each force.

force-magnitude.text: Check the sizes: constant speed means the forces balance.

extra-force.text: One of your forces has no matching interaction. Check every force has a real agent.

generic.text: Press Play: if the forces are right, the box keeps moving at a constant speed.

workedSolution.text: Weight: {{W}} N straight down, from the Earth.
Tension: {{T}} N along the rope, {{ang}}° above the horizontal.
Normal force: the forces balance vertically, so N = mg − T sin {{ang}}° = {{N}} N, up.
Friction: the forces balance horizontally, so f = T cos {{ang}}° = {{f}} N, backwards. The net force is zero: press Play to see constant velocity.

missing-normal.front: A box on a floor: which force stops it sinking into the floor?
missing-normal.back: The normal force from the floor, perpendicular to the surface.

missing-friction.front: A box pulled at constant speed on a rough floor: what balances the pull?
missing-friction.back: Kinetic friction from the floor, opposite the motion.

extra-force-of-motion.front: Is there a 'force of motion' on a moving box?
extra-force-of-motion.back: No. Motion continues by inertia; only forces with agents act.

normal-equals-weight.front: A rope pulls a box partly upward. Is N = mg?
normal-equals-weight.back: No. N = mg − T sin θ: the rope carries part of the weight.

constant-velocity-unbalanced.front: Constant velocity: what is the net force?
constant-velocity-unbalanced.back: Zero. All forces balance (Newton's first law).

missing-weight.front: Which force acts on every body near the Earth?

missing-tension.front: Which way does a rope pull?
missing-tension.back: Along the rope, away from the body.

generic.back: Gravity first, then one force per contact; check the net force matches the motion.
